newsitem.title: CHINA: China, Glencore ties seen threatened by dispute.
newsitem.headline: China, Glencore ties seen threatened by dispute.

text.p: Chinese state metals units and Swiss trading house Glencore were said by industry sources to be still trying to resolve a dispute that arose over the quality of Chinese zinc and could threaten long-standing links between them.

Glencore began talks on Sunday with China National Nonferrous Metals Industry Corp (CNNC) and China National Nonferrous Metals Import Export Corp (CNIEC) but no resolution had yet been reached, a source involved in the meetings said.
"We are in talks with Glencore but it is still too early to say anything because we have not achieved a final result," he said.
But CNNC and CNIEC were said by other trade sources to be close to severing ties with the Swiss company.

Dispute arose after Glencore complained to the London Metal Exchange (LME) about the quality of 100 tonnes of LME-registered Torch brand zinc ingots produced by the Zhuzhou smelter, a CNNC subsidiary, a Chinese trader said.

LME registration is an indication of internationally accepted standards of quality, packaging and reliability of delivery. China's three major smelters, Zhuzhou, Huludao and Shaoguan, make registered special high grade zinc brands Torch, HX and NH respectively.
The Chinese trader said an independent assessment of the zinc found no quality problems and that this particular dispute had been solved.
But according to other sources, including an official of the Zhuzhou smelter, differences had arisen from the dispute that still eluded solution.
"We have always maintained friendly ties with foreign clients, but if someone really adopts a non-cooperative attitude, we will not be responsible for the outcome," the official said.

Zhuzhou officials have denied pushing production up to 110-120 percent over annual capacity of 250,000 tonnes to take advantage of the high prices, saying they sell on long-term contracts and that the current market is good for them.

Industry sources have said Glencore customers began to complain about the quality of Torch zinc early in 1997, when the smelter raised output to take advantage of rising prices and duty-free Japanese imports.
